what: 1. Solving an ODE from a deSolve model
title: Getting started with pinnr
text: classic SIR epidemic model, written exactly deSolve::ode(): pinn_ode() turns PINN problem. initial state built network, equation learned. Epidemics start handful cases hard PINNs long horizons: network can find nearly flat curve small residual. Splitting time range windows training sequence (“time marching”) avoids . Compare deSolve:
code: sir <- function(t, y, parms) {   with(as.list(c(y, parms)), {     dS <- -beta * S * I     dI <- beta * S * I - gamma * I     dR <- gamma * I     list(c(dS, dI, dR))   }) } y0 <- c(S = 0.99, I = 0.01, R = 0) parms <- c(beta = 0.3, gamma = 0.1) times <- seq(0, 100, by = 1) prob <- pinn_ode(sir, y0 = y0, times = times, parms = parms) prob #> <pinn_problem> #>   Domain:     time in [0, 100] #>   Outputs:    S, I, R #>   Parameters: beta = 0.3, gamma = 0.1 #>   Output transform: yes fit <- pinn_fit(prob, windows = 5, seed = 1) fit #> <pinn_fit> #>   Outputs S, I, R on time in [0, 100] #>   Network 1-32-32-32-3, tanh activation #>   Time marching over 5 windows #>   Trained 5000 Adam steps per window in 235.4 s #>   Final loss (worst window) 4.735e-08 (residual 4.735e-08, conditions 0, data 0) ref <- as.data.frame(deSolve::ode(y0, times, sir, parms)) pred <- predict(fit) max(abs(as.matrix(pred[c("S", "I", "R")]) - as.matrix(ref[c("S", "I", "R")]))) #> [1] 0.002089985  plot(fit, type = "solution") lines(ref$time, ref$I, lty = 2)

title: Getting started with pinnr
text: Suppose observe infected recovered fractions every five days, measurement noise, want estimate beta gamma. Give starting guesses unknown observations data. derivative function unchanged; beta gamma now learned. true values beta = 0.3 gamma = 0.1. estimates’ path training useful judging convergence:  Observations cover every state: S never observed. Missing values (NA) data also ignored, different states can measured different times.
code: set.seed(42) obs <- ref[ref$time %% 5 == 0, c("time", "I", "R")] obs$I <- obs$I + rnorm(nrow(obs), sd = 0.005) obs$R <- obs$R + rnorm(nrow(obs), sd = 0.005) head(obs) #>    time          I            R #> 1     0 0.01685479 -0.008906542 #> 6     5 0.02353904  0.007607310 #> 11   10 0.06721241  0.036184205 #> 16   15 0.14465968  0.089668878 #> 21   20 0.24189748  0.173530409 #> 26   25 0.29943608  0.312187441 inv <- pinn_ode(sir, y0 = y0, times = times,                 unknown = c(beta = 0.5, gamma = 0.2), data = obs) fit_inv <- pinn_fit(inv, epochs = 5000, seed = 1) coef(fit_inv) #>       beta      gamma  #> 0.29416921 0.09781107 plot(fit_inv, type = "parameters") abline(h = c(0.3, 0.1), lty = 3)

title: Getting started with pinnr
text: PDEs, describe domain, residual conditions directly. residual ordinary R function whose arguments matched name outputs (u), variables (x, t) parameters (). function d() takes derivatives: d(u, t) ∂u/∂t\partial u/\partial t d(u, x, x) ∂2u/∂x2\partial^2 u / \partial x^2. heat equation ut=auxxu_t = \,u_{xx} 0≤x≤10 \le x \le 1, u(x,0)=sin⁡(πx)u(x, 0) = \sin(\pi x) u=0u = 0 ends, exact solution u=e−aπ2tsin⁡(πx)u = e^{-\pi^2 t}\sin(\pi x).  residuals() shows equation satisfied least well, useful diagnostic exact solution available:
code: heat <- pinn_problem(   domain = pinn_domain(x = c(0, 1), t = c(0, 1)),   outputs = "u",   residual = function(u, x, t, a, d) d(u, t) - a * d(u, x, x),   conditions = list(     pinn_initial(function(x) sin(pi * x), time = "t"),     pinn_dirichlet(where = list(x = "both"), value = 0)   ),   parms = list(a = 0.1) ) fit_heat <- pinn_fit(heat, epochs = 5000, seed = 1)  grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 51), t = seq(0, 1, length.out = 51)) pred <- predict(fit_heat, grid) max(abs(pred$u - exp(-0.1 * pi^2 * grid$t) * sin(pi * grid$x))) #> [1] 0.006326235 plot(fit_heat, type = "solution") res <- residuals(fit_heat, grid) summary(abs(res$residual_u)) #>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max.  #> 9.127e-06 4.437e-03 5.434e-03 5.858e-03 6.983e-03 4.144e-02

what: Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Native R with torch
title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Native R with torch
text: Physics-informed neural networks native R. pinnr trains neural networks satisfy differential equations. Use solve ordinary partial differential equations, estimate unknown parameters model observations. runs R’s torch, Python dependency, accepts ODE models written deSolve without changes.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks in Native R with torch
text: R excellent classical solvers differential equations, physics-informed neural networks far required Python libraries DeepXDE, R packages built single application. pinnr provides general, R-native interface: Use deSolve models directly. pinn_ode() takes function(t, y, parms) already wrote. Estimate parameters data. List unknown constants supply observations; learned network. States can partly observed, different times, missing values. Write PDEs R functions. Residuals plain functions arguments matched name, d(u, x, x) derivatives. Conditions real problems. Dirichlet, Neumann, initial custom (Robin, periodic, …) conditions, plus exact “hard” constraints output transforms. Practical training. Adam followed optional L-BFGS, Latin hypercube sampling resampling, time marching long ODE horizons, GPU support, reproducible seeds, stopping early Esc without losing model.

code: library(pinnr)  sir <- function(t, y, parms) {   with(as.list(c(y, parms)), {     dS <- -beta * S * I     dI <- beta * S * I - gamma * I     dR <- gamma * I     list(c(dS, dI, dR))   }) } y0 <- c(S = 0.99, I = 0.01, R = 0)  # simulate observations of I and R with deSolve ref <- as.data.frame(deSolve::ode(y0, 0:100, sir, c(beta = 0.3, gamma = 0.1))) obs <- ref[ref$time %% 5 == 0, c("time", "I", "R")]  prob <- pinn_ode(sir, y0 = y0, times = 0:100,                  unknown = c(beta = 0.5, gamma = 0.2), data = obs) fit <- pinn_fit(prob, epochs = 5000, seed = 1) coef(fit) #>  beta gamma #> ~0.30 ~0.10

title: Train a physics-informed neural network — pinn_fit
text: Fits fully connected network pinn_problem() (problem pinn_ode()) minimising $$w_r L_{residual} + w_c L_{conditions} + w_d L_{data},$$ term mean squared error. Training runs epochs steps Adam , optionally, lbfgs_iter iterations L-BFGS, often sharpens solution considerably.

title: Train a physics-informed neural network — pinn_fit
code: pinn_fit(   problem,   hidden = c(32, 32, 32),   activation = "tanh",   epochs = 5000,   lr = 0.001,   lr_unknown = NULL,   lbfgs_iter = 0,   n_collocation = 1000,   sampling = c("lhs", "uniform"),   resample_every = 0,   weights = c(residual = 1, conditions = 1, data = 1),   precision = c("float32", "float64"),   device = "cpu",   seed = NULL,   verbose = interactive(),   record_every = 10,   windows = 1 )

title: Train a physics-informed neural network — pinn_fit
text: problem pinn_problem. hidden Integer vector hidden layer widths. activation Activation function; see pinn_mlp(). epochs Number Adam steps. lr Adam learning rate network weights. lr_unknown Adam learning rate unknown parameters. Defaults 10 * lr. lbfgs_iter Number L-BFGS iterations Adam (0 skip). n_collocation Number points inside domain residual evaluated. sampling "lhs" (Latin hypercube) "uniform". resample_every Draw new collocation condition points every many Adam steps (0 keeps one fixed set). Resampling reduces overfitting training points. weights Named numeric vector loss weights residual, conditions data. Missing names default 1. precision "float32" (default) "float64". Double precision slower can help L-BFGS reach smaller losses. device torch device, "cpu", "cuda" "mps". seed Optional integer seed reproducible sampling weights. verbose Print progress messages. record_every Store loss every many steps. windows Number time windows ODE problems; see Long time horizons.

title: Train a physics-informed neural network — pinn_fit
text: defaults solve small problems CPU seconds minutes. loss stalls, try epochs, wider deeper network, collocation points, lbfgs_iter = 500. parameter estimation, larger lr_unknown lets parameters move faster network weights. Long time horizons hard PINNs; shorter windows, data, help.

title: Train a physics-informed neural network — pinn_fit
text: PINNs often converge wrong, flat solution ODE solved long horizon fast early dynamics (example epidemic starting cases). problems pinn_ode(), windows = k splits time range k equal windows trains one network per window, starting end state previous one ("time marching"). available forward problems (unknown parameters). Pressing Esc (Ctrl+C) stops training early returns model trained far, warning. loss becomes NaN infinite, training stops weights lowest loss seen far returned, also warning (diverged = TRUE result).

text: default initial state enforced exactly writing state \(y(t) = y_0 + \frac{t - t_0}{t_1 - t_0} N(t)\), \(N\) network. removes one loss term usually speeds training. Set hard_initial = FALSE use soft penalty instead.

title: Predict from a fitted PINN — predict.pinn_fit
code: decay <- function(t, y, parms) list(-parms["k"] * y) prob <- pinn_ode(decay, y0 = c(y = 1), times = c(0, 5), parms = c(k = 0.5)) fit <- pinn_fit(prob, hidden = c(16, 16), epochs = 1000, seed = 1) predict(fit, data.frame(time = c(0, 1, 2))) #>   time         y #> 1    0 1.0000000 #> 2    1 0.6344568 #> 3    2 0.3608426

title: pinnr 0.1.1
text: Fixed intermittent NaN wrong losses precision = "float64". Coordinate data tensors built one-column R matrices, torch_tensor() copy double precision, point memory R already freed. pinnr now always copies R data tensors. failure seen often Apple Silicon Macs. README: Intel Macs macOS 14 older need torch 0.16.3 earlier.

title: pinnr 0.1.0
text: First release. pinn_fit() longer throws away model loss becomes NaN infinite. keeps weights lowest loss seen far, restores , returns fit warning diverged = TRUE. Output columns data observed values now dropped instead making data loss NaN. happen windows, window sees slice data. plot(fit, type = "solution") draws 1D solutions dense grid, ODE curves smooth even times points. Window fits longer store copy whole problem call. pinn_sample() (therefore conditions) uses every combination fixed values several variables fixed, e.g. four corners = list(x = "", y = ""), gives every fixed value least one point. Argument checks reject NA hidden infinite counts rates clear messages. pinn_ode() builds problems deSolve-style ODE models, exact initial conditions default. pinn_problem() pinn_domain() define PDE problems rectangular domains; residuals R functions arguments matched name derivative operator d(). Conditions: pinn_dirichlet(), pinn_neumann(), pinn_initial() pinn_condition(), plus output transforms hard constraints. Parameter estimation partly observed, noisy data unknown data. pinn_fit() trains Adam optional L-BFGS, Latin hypercube sampling, resampling, time marching (windows) long ODE horizons, GPU devices single double precision. Methods predict(), residuals(), coef(), plot(), summary(), pinn_save() / pinn_load().
